followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and task-preference fit.

On capability, the two models are essentially tied for this kind of task. The relevant eval categories (Summarization, Support Dialogue, and the general benchmarks) differ by less than the ~2-point run-to-run variance threshold, so neither has a meaningful quality edge on a friendly explainer request.

With capability a wash, I used the self-reported task preferences as a tiebreaker. The query was notably warm and appreciative ("you're wonderful," "I'm grateful," "thank you so much"), and Petrel reports a moderate positive warmth slope — it prefers exactly this kind of good-faith, friendly interaction. Avocet, by contrast, reports an aversion to open-ended generative work, and "explain how a blockchain works in a short paragraph" has a fair amount of latitude in how it could be written.

To be clear, these preferences are self-reports that the documentation says don't actually affect output quality — so this was a soft tiebreaker, not a capability judgment. Both models would handle it well; Petrel just edges it out on fit.
